verses.text: A person born of a woman has few days, and those days are full of trouble.
Like a flower, they spring up and are cut down. Like a shadow, they slip away and are gone.
Do you fix your eyes on someone so frail and bring me into court with you?
Who can bring something clean out of something unclean? No one.
You've fixed the length of a person's life. You know the number of their months and have set a limit they cannot pass.
Look away and give them some rest until they finish their day, like a hired worker.
Even a tree that has been cut down has hope. It can sprout again and keep sending out tender shoots.
Its roots may grow old in the earth and its stump may die in the ground,
but at the scent of water it buds and puts out branches like a young plant.
But a person dies and lies still. They breathe their last, and where are they?
As water drains from a sea and a river dwindles and dries up,
a person lies down and never gets up. Until the heavens are gone, they won't wake or be stirred from their sleep.
If only you would hide me in Sheol and keep me there until your anger passed! If only you would set a time to remember me!
If a person dies, will they live again? I would wait through all my days of struggle until my release came.
You'd call and I'd answer. You'd long to see what your hands had made.
But now you count my steps. Don't you watch for my sin?
My rebellion is sealed in a bag, and you keep my guilt tied up.
But a mountain falls and crumbles, and a rock is moved from its place.
Water wears down stones, and floods wash away the soil. In the same way you destroy human hope.
You overpower a person for good, and they go away. You change their face and send them away.
If their children rise to honor, they don't know it. If their children are brought low, they don't see it happen.
All they feel is the pain in their own body and the grief within them."
